articleSummary: Indonesia's Health Ministry says hepatitis B risk remains high despite immunisation. More than 60% of the population is susceptible; the vaccination program has sharply reduced transmission among children. articleSummary: COVID-19 has risen to a moderate level of community transmission nationwide in week 29 (July 13–19, 2026), with sentinel hospital positivity at 16.3%. The dominant strain remains NB.1.8.1 (XDV) lineage; no new variants with increased public health risk detected. Most infections are mild and present with upper-respiratory symptoms: sore throat, cough, fever; some patients have loss of smell or taste, nasal congestion, diarrhea, or conjunctivitis. High-risk groups—elderly, those with chronic diseases, and immunocompromised—remain vulnerable; early diagnosis and antiviral treatment are advised for symptomatic high-risk individuals. Wuhan shows moderate intensity, more children affected, and no severe cases or deaths reported; circulating strain is still NB.1.8.1. The rise is not strongly seasonal, attributed to waning immunity and indoor air-conditioned environments with summer travel. Protective measures include masking in priority settings, hand hygiene, ventilation, healthy living, and stricter surveillance in high-risk venues like summer schools and eldercare facilities.
notes: COVID-19は既に定着した疾患であり、本記事は中国当局による定例的な流行状況アップデート（サーベイランスレポート）。新規変異株や重症化増加の兆候はなく、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
